  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the connection of "Atah Echad" to the Minchah prayer of Shabbat, the third meal, and the two modes of inclusion (from below to above and above to below) as exemplified by Yaakov's dream.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, one can explain the connection of "Atah Echad" to the Minchah prayer of Shabbat, which is the ratzon ha'ratzonim (will of wills).</t>
    <t s="2">For it is known</t>
    <t s="3">regarding the matter of the three meals of Shabbat,</t>
    <t s="4">that the third meal of Shabbat is the aspect of the essential delight that has no hold on any thing,</t>
    <t s="5">therefore it is said of it,</t>
    <t s="6">"Today not,"</t>
    <t s="7">similar to the aspect of the World to Come, in which there is neither eating nor drinking.</t>
    <t s="8">And based on this, it will be understood why specifically then we say "Atah Echad... and who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land,"</t>
    <t s="9">because through the drawing down of the aspect of essential delight,</t>
    <t s="10">similar to the aspect of "before Havayah,"</t>
    <t s="11">the true matter of inclusion in the souls of Israel is effected,</t>
    <t s="12">and through this, the aspect of "Echad" (One) is drawn down even in the land.</t>
    <t s="13">And this is also the meaning of what is written, "And he placed it as a pillar and poured oil on its head,"</t>
    <t s="14">for it was explained above</t>
    <t s="15">(in the maamar "Atem Nitzavim" earlier,</t>
    <t s="16">chapter 6)</t>
    <t s="17">that regarding the matter of inclusion, there are two modes,</t>
    <t s="18">from below to above and from above to below.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is "And he took the stone... and placed it as a pillar,"</t>
    <t s="20">"And he took... and placed it as a pillar" is in the manner of elevation</t>
    <t s="21">from below to above</t>
    <t s="22">(similar to "Atem Nitzavim" on Rosh Hashanah),</t>
    <t s="23">for after this, from the "stones of the place" (plural) it became one stone,</t>
    <t s="24">he elevated it from below to above until it became a pillar,</t>
    <t s="25">and afterwards, "and he poured oil on its head,"</t>
    <t s="26">a drawing down from above to below</t>
    <t s="27">(similar to the inclusion that comes from the elevation of Yom Kippur),</t>
    <t s="28">through which the aspect of unity and inclusion is drawn down even to the very lowest place,</t>
    <t s="29">and this is the matter of "and he poured oil on its head,"</t>
    <t s="30">for oil permeates throughout.</t>
    <t s="31">And through the drawing down of unity even to the lowest place,</t>
    <t s="32">which is the refinement of the sparks that are in the lower things</t>
    <t s="33">[and this is also the matter of the condition,</t>
    <t s="34">"If God will be with me...",</t>
    <t s="35">for all this relates to the matter of refinements,</t>
    <t s="36">as explained in Torah Ohr there, chapter 9],</t>
    <t s="37">behold, through this, "and this stone... shall be a house of God,"</t>
    <t s="38">for these refinements will add elevation and perfection to the Name Elokim,</t>
    <t s="39">and also to the Name Havayah, as in "Havayah will be for Him as Elokim,"</t>
    <t s="40">because through this, the intention that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place in the lower realms is completed.</t>
    <t s="41">And since this intention is in His essential Self</t>
    <t s="42">[for this is what the Alter Rebbe said, "On a desire, there is no question,"</t>
    <t s="43">for in His essential Self, the matter of reason, etc., does not apply],</t>
    <t s="44">therefore, the completion of this intention adds also to the aspect of Havayah, as in "Havayah will be for Him as Elokim."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects "Atah Echad" to the 9th of Kislev, explaining that the power to draw unity into the land comes from the aspect of "before Havayah," as seen in the Mitteler Rebbe's passing and his discourse on "Ki imcha mekor chayim."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, one can explain the connection of "Atah Echad... one nation in the land" to the 9th and 10th of Kislev.</t>
    <t s="2">For the words of the Tzemach Tzedek are known</t>
    <t s="3">regarding the passing of the Mitteler Rebbe: "Such a passing has not been found since the day of the passing of Rashbi, of blessed memory,"</t>
    <t s="4">and as recounted in the introduction to Torah Ohr from the son of the Mitteler Rebbe, that "he expounded for an hour or more until he reached the verse,</t>
    <t s="5">'For with You is the source of life...'</t>
    <t s="6">the holy luminary did not finish saying 'life.'"</t>
    <t s="7">(As is said</t>
    <t s="8">regarding the passing of Rashbi.)</t>
    <t s="9">And it is known</t>
    <t s="10">in the explanation of the verse "For with You is the source of life,"</t>
    <t s="11">that the aspect of "source of life" is only "with You,"</t>
    <t s="12">subordinate and nullified to You.</t>
    <t s="13">From this it is understood that what the baal hahilula (master of the celebration) then said, the verse "For with You is the source of life," is similar to "in one knot I am bound,"</t>
    <t s="14">for relative to this aspect,</t>
    <t s="15">the aspect of "source of life" is subordinate and nullified.</t>
    <t s="16">And based on this, the connection of "Atah Echad... one nation in the land" to the 9th of Kislev will be understood,</t>
    <t s="17">for the power to draw down the aspect of "Echad" even into matters of the land,</t>
    <t s="18">comes from the aspect of "before Havayah"</t>
    <t s="19">(as above in the maamar "Atem Nitzavim"),</t>
    <t s="20">and also the matters of the land that are refined and included in the aspect of "Echad" reach His essential Self</t>
    <t s="21">(as above in the explanation of "and this stone... shall be a house of God").</t>
    <t s="22">And this is also the connection of "Atah Echad" to the matter of the redemption,</t>
    <t s="23">for it is known</t>
    <t s="24">"that the news of the redemption came on Shabbat, the 9th of Kislev, at the time of Minchah, when the Mitteler Rebbe said the Chassidic discourse beginning with the words 'Atah Echad,'"</t>
    <t s="25">for through</t>
    <t s="26">(the saying of this discourse on Shabbat at the time of Minchah,</t>
    <t s="27">the ratzon ha'ratzonim)</t>
    <t s="28">which effects the drawing down of "Echad" in the land,</t>
    <t s="29">the aspect of "in multitudes they were with me,"</t>
    <t s="30">behold, through this, "He redeemed my soul in peace" is effected.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the lesson for each person, especially those involved in spreading the wellsprings outward, connecting the work of the Mitteler Rebbe (Binah) to the drawing down of unity in the land and the ultimate redemption.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is also a lesson for each and every one who walks in His ways,</t>
    <t s="2">and especially for those who are engaged in the work of "spreading your wellsprings outward,"</t>
    <t s="3">for this was the matter of the Mitteler Rebbe,</t>
    <t s="4">and as is known,</t>
    <t s="5">that the Mitteler Rebbe is the matter of the Sefirah of Binah,</t>
    <t s="6">therefore he said Chassidic discourses in a manner of expansion and broadening,</t>
    <t s="7">"the broad spaces of the river" of Binah,</t>
    <t s="8">and the revelation of Atik is in Binah.</t>
    <t s="9">And from the broadening of Binah</t>
    <t s="10">(and especially from the revelation of Atik within Binah),</t>
    <t s="11">the revelation is drawn down even below,</t>
    <t s="12">the spreading of the wellsprings outward,</t>
    <t s="13">the drawing down of the aspect of "Echad" in the land</t>
    <t s="14">[And based on this, one can explain in the discourse itself, that when the Mitteler Rebbe said the aforementioned discourse "Atah Echad,"</t>
    <t s="15">he paused in his saying and said, "Sha,</t>
    <t s="16">make room, the father is here,"</t>
    <t s="17">for the Alter Rebbe is the matter of the Sefirah of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="18">and Chochmah and Binah are two companions that never separate,</t>
    <t s="19">therefore, at the time he said the discourse "Atah Echad... one in the land,"</t>
    <t s="20">the matter of the broadening of Binah,</t>
    <t s="21">the Alter Rebbe was also present then,</t>
    <t s="22">the Sefirah of Chochmah],</t>
    <t s="23">behold, through the work of "spreading your wellsprings outward,"</t>
    <t s="24">and as is known,</t>
    <t s="25">that the Mitteler Rebbe wanted,</t>
    <t s="26">that when two young men meet, they should speak about the matter of Arich and Atik, etc.,</t>
    <t s="27">for this is the matter of spreading the wellsprings outward,</t>
    <t s="28">that even when the wellsprings come outward, they remain "wellsprings,"</t>
    <t s="29">behold, through this, "He redeemed my soul in peace" is effected,</t>
    <t s="30">a private redemption,</t>
    <t s="31">and from this one comes afterwards also to the general redemption,</t>
    <t s="32">and even to the true and complete redemption,</t>
    <t s="33">when there will be the true unity and inclusion,</t>
    <t s="34">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="35">"And they shall no longer teach, each man his fellow"</t>
    <t s="36">(and as explained in the aforementioned maamar "Atem Nitzavim"),</t>
    <t s="37">for the earth will be filled with knowledge of Havayah as the waters cover the sea.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
